notes.purpose: jaxfne/vis/plotly is the Plotly-backend visualization pipeline for jaxfne. Per its own module docstring (jaxfne/vis/plotly/__init__.py lines 1-11): "Generic, package-native, manuscript-agnostic. Every function takes a jaxfne.Signals (and usually a jaxfne.Model) and returns a plotly.graph_objects.Figure — no manuscript-specific preprocessing." It is organized as one file per plot concern (network.py, raster.py, lfp.py, csd.py, spectra.py, connectivity.py, metrics.py) + a shared internal helper module (_common.py) + an assembled multi-panel dashboard (dashboard.py) + export helpers (exporters.py) + a separate `manuscript/` sub-package that layers manuscript-specific figure recipes (figure0..figure4.py) on top of the generic primitives.
key_findings: 11 top-level .py files + a manuscript/ subdir with 6 files (__init__.py, figure0-4.py); total non-manuscript .py size sums to 643 lines per `wc -l` (exporters.py 6, csd.py 29, metrics.py 29, __init__.py 43, lfp.py 46, connectivity.py 47, dashboard.py 63, _common.py 82, raster.py 92, network.py 95, spectra.py 111).

__init__.py (lines 24-43) declares __all__ with 16 names: plot_network_3d, plot_raster, plot_population_rates, plot_membrane_potentials, plot_lfp, plot_csd, plot_psd, plot_spectrogram, plot_band_power, plot_depth_profile, plot_connectivity, plot_objective_history, create_dashboard, export_figure, export_figures, FigureBundle, manuscript_figures, manuscript -- this is the real public surface.

_common.py line 1 docstring: 'Shared helpers for the Plotly visualization pipeline. Not public API.' -- it is not imported into __init__.py's __all__, confirming it is internal-only (helpers: require_plotly, neuron_table_arrays, field_proxy, contact_depths_mm, time_ms, dt_ms, population_rate_hz, color_for_cell_types).

dashboard.py's create_dashboard (lines 12-63) assembles network/raster/rates/lfp/csd/psd/depth_profile panels into one 3x3 plotly subplot figure via make_subplots, and can write standalone HTML (output_html arg, line 40 write_html with include_plotlyjs='cdn').

manuscript/__init__.py (lines 1-27) documents manuscript_figures(signals, model, *, perturbation_signals=None, hierarchy_signals=None) building a 5-figure FigureBundle (figure0_background .. figure4_hierarchical_manipulations), explicitly built on the generic Plotly primitives, not the other way around.

Proxy-readout caveat is stated twice: __init__.py lines 7-10 and dashboard.py lines 15-16 -- LFP/CSD/source fields are *_proxy fields from the linear laminar-source kernel and the plotting code is documented to never escalate that claim.
contracts: AGENTS.md line 106: 'Plotting: `jaxfne/vis/*` only (modular-grammar rule 2).' -- confirmed verbatim in /Users/hamednejat/workspace/analysis/jaxfne/AGENTS.md; all plotting code in the repo must live under jaxfne/vis/*, and this subpackage (jaxfne/vis/plotly/) is one of its backends.

_common.require_plotly() (lines 15-21) is the lazy-import guard pattern used before touching the `plotly` package -- raises a clear ImportError with install instructions rather than failing on a bare `import plotly` at module load, so plotly stays an optional dependency.

Every plotting function's real signature takes a Signals object (and usually a Model) and returns a plotly.graph_objects.Figure, per the __init__.py docstring contract (lines 3-5) -- no manuscript-specific args leak into the generic primitives.

Field proxy naming is fixed by _common.field_proxy's dict (lines 42-47): short keys 'lfp'/'csd'/'phi_e'/'source' map to signals.field.{lfp,csd,phi_e,source}_proxy attributes -- any new consumer of signals.field should use this mapping rather than re-deriving attribute names.
